Since \(A=(-\infty,-1)\cup(3,\infty)\), the only gap in \(A\) is \([-1,3]\).  
Thus \(A\cup B=\mathbb{R}\) requires \(B\supseteq[-1,3]\).

Also \(A\cap B=(3,4]\), so \(B\) must extend to include \((3,4]\) but cannot include anything beyond \(4\) or below \(-1\). Hence

\[
B=[-1,4].
\]

Therefore \(x^2+ax+b\le 0\) has roots \(-1\) and \(4\):

\[
x^2+ax+b=(x+1)(x-4)=x^2-3x-4.
\]

So \(a=-3\), \(b=-4\), and

\[
a+b=-7.
\]

\[
\boxed{-7}
\]
